prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

(CNN)  -- Rock group R.E.M. debuted a song from its upcoming album Wednesday on CNN's "Anderson Cooper 360°" program. R.E.M. singer Michael Stipe says the band was honored to be involved with the "Planet in Peril" project. The song "Until the Day Is Done" also will appear later this month in "Planet in Peril," a four-hour CNN documentary that looks at environmental crises around the world. "With 'Planet in Peril,' Anderson Cooper and his team have done an amazing job capturing global eco-devastation," said R.E.M singer Michael Stipe in a news release. "The images in the film are beautiful, while at the same time heartbreaking and frightening. We are honored to have our song included in this monumental project." This isn't the first time R.E.M. has worked with Cooper. The band premiered its video "Bad Day" on the show in 2002. "Planet in Peril" executive producer Charlie Moore said the group's longstanding commitment to environmental causes made them a natural choice for the project.  Watch a trailer for "Planet in Peril" and hear "Until the Day Is Done" » . Moore said they contacted R.E.M. earlier this year to see if the group would be willing to write a song to go with the documentary, and the band happened to be in the studio working on their upcoming album. "We were able to hear some of the stuff they were doing and this particular song fits perfectly for the project," Moore said. He said the group, their management and their record label were eager to be involved. "It's sort of serendipitous that we were able to work something out with them," Moore said. "All the stars were lined up for this to happen, they were in the studio, they were working on a song that fit with the feeling that the pictures portray and they really match up very well. And we like their music, we like their work and are just thrilled that they wanted to be a part of it." "Planet in Peril" features CNN anchor Anderson Cooper, chief medical correspondent Dr. Sanjay Gupta and "Animal Planet" host and wildlife biologist Jeff Corwin. The two-part documentary was filmed in 13 countries and focuses on the issues of climate change, deforestation, species loss and overpopulation. CNN will air "Planet in Peril" on October 23 and 24 at 9 p.m.  ET. It also will be broadcast on CNN International. In a message on the R.E.M.'s Web site, the group said it had finished recording songs for the new album, which is scheduled to be released next year. The band also is releasing a live CD/DVD on Tuesday with 22-tracks recorded at a 2005 concert in Dublin, Ireland. E-mail to a friend .

# R.E.M. debuts new song for CNN’s ‘Planet in Peril’

**By CNN Entertainment**

R.E.M. has added its voice to the conversation about the planet’s future.

The veteran alternative-rock band debuted “Until the Day Is Done” on CNN’s **“Anderson Cooper 360°,”** pairing the reflective new song with images from **“Planet in Peril,”** the network’s environmental documentary.

Anchored by Anderson Cooper and featuring reports from CNN chief medical correspondent Dr. Sanjay Gupta and wildlife expert Jeff Corwin, “Planet in Peril” examines environmental threats around the world, including deforestation, disappearing species and the effects of climate change.

“Until the Day Is Done” offers an appropriately somber soundtrack. Michael Stipe’s restrained vocals and the band’s spare arrangement underscore the documentary’s sense of urgency, while its lyrics focus on responsibility, consequence and an uncertain future.

The appearance gave viewers an early listen to new material from R.E.M., whose members have long supported environmental and social causes. Rather than staging a conventional performance, the band allowed the song to unfold alongside footage of landscapes, wildlife and communities affected by ecological change.

The collaboration also marked an unusual meeting of music and television journalism, using an original song to extend the documentary’s message beyond scientific findings and on-the-ground reporting.

“Planet in Peril” follows Cooper, Gupta and Corwin as they travel to environmental hot spots and investigate how human activity is reshaping the natural world. R.E.M.’s contribution closes the distance between those global concerns and the personal question at the heart of the special: What will be left for future generations?

**ATLANTA —** R.E.M. has teamed with CNN on *Planet in Peril*, a two-part documentary examining the environmental threats confronting communities and ecosystems around the world.

The collaboration features “Until the Day Is Done,” a song from R.E.M.’s album *Accelerate*, alongside footage from the documentary. Michael Stipe said the band welcomed the opportunity to connect its music with the project, describing the environment as “the most important issue of our time.”

CNN executive producer Charlie Moore said R.E.M.’s history of social and environmental engagement made the group a fitting creative partner. He called the band “a natural fit” for a documentary intended to convey both the scale and urgency of the challenges facing the planet.

Led by CNN correspondents Anderson Cooper, Sanjay Gupta and Jeff Corwin, *Planet in Peril* reports from locations across several continents. The documentary explores climate change, deforestation, species loss, pollution and the pressures that population growth and human consumption place on natural resources. It also focuses on how environmental degradation affects public health and vulnerable communities.

The two-part special is scheduled to air on CNN on **October 23 and October 24**.
